source_frontmatter.name: food-analyzer
source_frontmatter.description: Analyze food photos, nutrition labels, and ingredient lists. Trigger on food images, nutrition label scans, macro questions, glycemic questions, medication interaction checks, and similar food-analysis requests.

transformations.If no image is attached and the request: If the request depends on an image that is not attached or usable, and the supplied text cannot support the requested analysis, stop before the analysis template. Return one short request that identifies the missing input, with at most one additional sentence if essential. For example: "Please upload the meal photo, or describe the food, ingredients and portions; no usable image or description was supplied." Adapt this request to the missing source. Omit a separate general nutrition disclaimer in this intake-only reply. Do not add nutrition tables, unknown-value inventories, formulas, report headings or execution checklists to this clarification. Do not invent image inspection or nutrition/allergen facts. This early return does not apply when a supplied label transcription or description already supports the task.
transformations.- Separate obvious observations from low:
- Separate obvious observations from low confidence guesses when the image or label is incomplete
- Use the FDA 2,000 kcal reference diet for percent daily values; label user-provided custom targets as percent of custom target, not FDA %DV
- Keep medication and supplement warnings factual and end that section with a pharmacist and physician disclaimer
transformations.- Dietary Fiber: 28g\n- Total Sugars: 50:
- Dietary Fiber: 28g
- Total Sugars: no FDA Daily Value; report grams only
- Added Sugars: 50g
- Protein: 50g
transformations.- Potassium: 4,700mg\n\n:
- Potassium: 4,700mg

Sugar reference checked 2026-11-03: [FDA Added Sugars on the Nutrition Facts Label](https://www.fda.gov/food/nutrition-facts-label/added-sugars-nutrition-facts-label). Added sugars are included in total sugars, not an extra amount to add to them.

Keep `total_sugars_g` and `added_sugars_g` separate. Calculate added-sugars %DV as `added_sugars_g / 50 * 100`. Never assign an FDA %DV to total sugars or infer added sugars from total sugars. If added sugars are not supplied, retain total sugar grams and report added sugars and their %DV as unknown, not zero.
transformations.- scale calories and macros linearly for:
- scale calories and macros linearly for half, double, or N-serving batches and show the per-serving and total lines
- scale supplied total and added sugar grams separately; recompute added-sugars %DV from the scaled grams, keep missing added sugars unknown, and keep total-sugars %DV not applicable
- do not scale glycemic load advice linearly without comment; portion size changes the practical impact, so note when a doubled portion moves the meal into a different GI burden category

transformations.## Output Sections\n\nInclude the sectio:
## Output Sections

For a complete single-food analysis, read [the report layout](references/report-layout.md) and follow its compact, labeled FOOD ANALYSIS format. Start with the food name, serving and confidence; put the practical bottom line after the report. Do not prepend a separate Quick Summary. Keep the missing-input early return above and adapt comparison/history requests to their own workflows.
transformations.## Output Expectations\n\nThe analysis s:
## Output Expectations

Use the report layout for the section order, field labels, spacing and conditional sections. Preserve the user's requested format and the host's rendering constraints; where a monospace report is unsuitable, use the same labels and order in plain text. Fill only supported fields, distinguishing label facts, estimates and unknowns. A screenshot of a prior assistant response is a layout reference, not a verified nutrition label or clinical source.
transformations.- [ ] Quick summary appears before deepe: - [ ] Food name, serving and confidence lead the report; the practical bottom line follows it
transformations.If uncertain between two NOVA groups, pr: If ingredients are incomplete, state a tentative classification or unknown with the reason; do not silently resolve uncertainty into a definitive score.
transformations.Estimate glycemic load as `(GI x net car: Estimate glycemic load as `(GI x available carbohydrate grams per serving) / 100` only when a defensible GI estimate and available carbohydrate amount exist. Identify the source or assumption; do not invent a measured GI for a mixed food from its label or appearance. Consider modifiers such as fiber, fat, protein, cooking method, ripeness, and food form without promising an individual glucose response.

references/report-layout.md.reason: Restore the user-requested historical report presentation while preserving evidence limits, FDA sugar distinctions and medical safety; no personal screenshots are distributed.
